candidates.summary: The Kenilworth Artists Association is a standing neighborhood artists' association in Asheville's Kenilworth neighborhood that runs an annual self-guided studio tour of 27 member artists. It maintains its own website with a yearly artist roster, volunteer coordination, and sponsorship pages, and donates 5% of tour sales to a fixed charity partner (Loving Food Resources) each year, indicating an organization that persists beyond a single event rather than a one-off tour brand.

candidates.name: 12 Baskets Cafe
candidates.notes: program of the Asheville Poverty Initiative

candidates.name: When the Old No Longer Fits
candidates.notes: supportive circle for women in transition

candidates.name: RSAA
candidates.notes: meets at the AmeriHealth Caritas NC Wellness Center

candidates.name: Living Wage Coalition of Transylvania County
Skeletons in the Closet: Queer Horror Book Club
East Asheville Library Evening Book Club
Asheville Pickleball Association
candidates.notes: runs Blue Ridge Pickleball at Harrah's Cherokee Center

candidates.name: Ikebana International Asheville Chapter #74
candidates.summary: Ikebana International Asheville is Chapter #74 of the worldwide nonprofit Ikebana International, a membership club practicing Japanese ikebana flower arrangement under its motto 'Friendship through Flowers.' It holds monthly member programs and demonstrations, seasonal luncheons, and friendship gatherings, with instruction across four ikebana schools (Ichiyo, Ikenobo, Ohara, Sogetsu). The NC Arboretum exhibition in the listing is a public showcase the chapter mounts, not the chapter itself, but confirms the same club that meets and teaches regularly.

candidates.name: Swannanoa Public Library Star Trek Fan Club
Swing Asheville
candidates.notes: Monday night swing classes; kept separate from Asheville Swing Night

candidates.name: Blue Ridge Audubon
candidates.summary: Blue Ridge Audubon is a chapter of the National Audubon Society serving Buncombe, Henderson, and surrounding WNC counties, run as a volunteer-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a board of directors, members, free program meetings, monthly bird outings, and sanctuary workdays. The listed event itself is a Swannanoa Valley Museum program ('History is for the Birds', $65, biweekly) merely led by a guide supplied by the chapter, not the chapter's own membership activity, but the chapter behind that guide is a genuine returning-member organization.
candidates.notes: chapter of the National Audubon Society

candidates.name: Asheville Gay Men's Chorus
candidates.summary: The Asheville Gay Men's Chorus is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit community chorus (legally Cantaria Inc. of Asheville) with a Board of Directors and Artistic Team, affiliated with GALA Choruses. It actively recruits and auditions new singers ('Join Your Voice to Ours!'), meaning it has a returning core membership of singers rather than a rotating public. The two listed events are performances by this standing chorus at a host venue, not the group itself.
aliases: Asheville Gay Men's Chorus (Cantaria Inc. of Asheville)

candidates.name: We Hike to Heal
candidates.notes: women's mindful hikes led by WH2H ambassadors

candidates.name: Womansong of Asheville
candidates.summary: Womansong of Asheville is a long-running community women's chorus that rehearses and performs together, with a director, an assistant director role, and standing committees (e.g. the New Start Fund grant committee). The 'Where the Hope Comes From' listing on this account is their ticketed spring concert, but the group itself is a persistent membership ensemble that recruits singers year-round via a 'Sing With Us' page, not a commercial promoter of one-off shows.

candidates.name: MTN VIBEZ
candidates.summary: MTN VIBEZ is DJ Mtn Vibez, run by Guillermo Moreno, who spins a weekly Latin Night at One World Brewing West every Wednesday (dance lesson 8:30-9pm, open dance 9pm-midnight, $10 cover) and also plays a Saturday 'Miami Nights' Latin set at Hemingway's Cuba. It is a paid, DJ-hosted brewery party open to the public, not a membership community; the attendees are a rotating crowd of dancers and nightlife patrons, while only the DJ/host is the constant.
candidates.notes: DJ Mtn Vibez's weekly Latin Night at One World Brewing West

candidates.name: Catawba Falls Group Hike
candidates.summary: This is a paid, guided commercial hiking tour run by Blue Ridge Hiking Co., whose downtown Asheville shop (70 College Street) is listed as the event's 'organizer' address. Each week's listing is a bookable tour capped at 6 participants, with round-trip transportation and snacks included; there is no indication of a returning membership or community identity among attendees, just paying customers on a guide-led trip.
aliases: Blue Ridge Hiking Co. - Catawba Falls Group Hike (guided tour)
candidates.notes: weekly guided hike run by Blue Ridge Hiking Co.

candidates.name: Pack Memorial Library LEGO Builders Club
candidates.summary: A weekly drop-in LEGO building session for grades K-5 at Pack Memorial Library in downtown Asheville, part of Buncombe County Public Libraries' after-school kids programming. The library supplies all the bricks and there is no sign-up, membership, or fixed roster; it's an open library activity, not a club with returning members who know each other.

candidates.name: Pisgah Sunday Jam
candidates.summary: A weekly Sunday-evening open jam on the taproom stage at Pisgah Brewing Company in Black Mountain, run by the venue itself rather than a standing community. Each week's listing names a different rotating host or featured touring act (Spiro & Friends, Alex Bazemore, etc.) and explicitly invites 'any and all musicians' to sit in, with no membership, dues, sign-up form, or dedicated group page anywhere in the descriptions.
candidates.notes: hosted by Spiro & Friends at Pisgah Brewing

candidates.name: Hi-Wire RAD Board Game Night
candidates.summary: A weekly house-hosted board game night at Hi-Wire Brewing's RAD Beer Garden taproom, part of the venue's regular weekly programming alongside 'Mug Mondays' and 'Trivia Tuesdays'. It's an open drop-in activity using the taproom's own game shelf plus BYO games, with no club name, membership, dues, or named organizer beyond the brewery itself.

candidates.name: BarCada
candidates.summary: BarCada is a multi-city commercial event company (umbrella of 'Ermantourage') running templated 'Dinner with Strangers' and 'Coffee with Strangers' event series in dozens of cities nationwide, not just Asheville. Each ticketed event ($23-$34) pairs two strangers one-on-one at a rotating restaurant or cafe based on a post-signup questionnaire about age, interests, and favorite foods; the 'Duos Edition' format is explicitly a one-time algorithmic pairing, not a returning membership.
candidates.notes: Dinner and Coffee with Strangers; Ermantourage umbrella

candidates.name: Shamrock Irons Jazz Jam
candidates.summary: A weekly Thursday night, 7-10pm, no-cover series at Shamrock Irons Irish Pub in downtown Asheville: a curated jazz showcase of booked/professional musicians (curator Steven Alvarez) followed by an open jam where 'qualified players' sit in. It reads as venue-run commercial programming rather than a self-organized community: musicians apply through the venue's own Artist Booking Form, and there is no membership language, named regulars, or independent group identity (Facebook group, Discord, etc.) separate from the pub's own event listings.
aliases: Jazz Showcase & Jam (curated by Steven Alvarez)
candidates.notes: Jazz Showcase & Jam curated by Steven Alvarez

candidates.name: Country Line Dance w/ Kristey
candidates.summary: A weekly Wednesday-night ($5) country line dance class at Eda's Hide-a-Way, a Weaverville bar, taught by an instructor named Kristey with separate beginner and advanced hours. Listings and the venue's own event page frame it as instruction ('get yourselves primed and ready for the dance floor at our weekend shows') rather than a club, with no membership, dues, sign-up, named regulars, or dedicated group social page found.

candidates.name: Community Drum Class with Larry McDowell
candidates.summary: A free, drop-in hand-drumming class taught weekly (Mondays) by instructor Larry McDowell at The Well, a West Asheville community event space. It is explicitly framed as beginner/intermediate friendly with no experience necessary and shared drums provided, not a membership-based community; only the instructor and venue recur.

candidates.name: Early Tuesday Jam
candidates.summary: A weekly Tuesday night music night at The One Stop (Asheville Music Hall) anchored by a fixed house band ("Trilateral Omission", featuring members of Empire Strikes Brass) that plays 8-10pm, followed by an open sit-in hour from 10-11pm explicitly open to "musicians from inside the AVL community and anywhere beyond." It reads as a band residency plus open-door jam, not a persistent membership community: no dues, sign-up roster, or club identity, and the sit-in segment is framed as welcoming any visiting musician rather than a returning known cohort.
candidates.notes: with Empire Strikes Brass at The One Stop

candidates.name: Sovereign Kava Ping Pong Tournament
candidates.summary: A weekly bracket-style ping pong tournament run by Sovereign Kava, a kava bar at 268 Biltmore Ave in Asheville, with free entry and no skill requirement. It is a venue-hosted bar night rather than a club: no league or club name, no membership or sign-up, and the table is open to walk-in play seven days a week beyond the tournament itself.

candidates.name: Weird Wednesday Open Jam
candidates.summary: A weekly Wednesday night at Sly Grog Lounge in Asheville billed as an 'anything-goes' electronic jam (synths, samplers, laptops, DJ gear) hosted by a DJ going by 'Disco Goddess.' It reads as a drop-in, DJ-led open-jam night for whoever shows up rather than a fixed community of returning members.

candidates.name: Miami Nights Latin Dance
candidates.summary: Miami Nights is a weekly Saturday-night Latin dance party thrown by Hemingway's Cuba, a rooftop bar inside the Cambria Downtown Asheville hotel: a free beginner salsa/bachata lesson from an outside dance company (Duarte Latin Dance / DuARTE), then DJ MTN Vibez spinning salsa, bachata, reggaeton and Latin house for social dancing until 1am. It reads as the venue's recurring promotional night (drink specials, bar bites, free admission) rather than a self-organized community with its own identity.

candidates.name: Well Played Blood on the Clocktower Group
candidates.summary: This is a $10 ticketed 'Social Deduction Showdown' session of Blood on the Clocktower run biweekly by Well Played Board Game Café in Asheville, capped at 15 players and 'hosted and guided by an experienced storyteller.' Every listing across both units reuses identical generic marketing copy ('Join us for another session of lies, secrets, and murder—can you survive the night?') with no membership language, no named regulars, and no mention of a dedicated club, Discord, or Facebook group for this specific offering. It reads as a commercial recurring game-night product run by the café's staff storyteller, with a rotating paying public rather than a self-organizing community.

candidates.name: RAD Brewing Game Night
candidates.summary: A weekly board-and-video-game night hosted in-house by River Arts District Brewing Co. (13 Mystery St, Asheville) alongside its own food truck and beer, run by the brewery itself rather than by an independent club. There is no named organizing group, membership language, or dedicated Facebook/Meetup presence tied to it, and the descriptions are identical each week, indicating it's a venue promotion rather than a returning community.

candidates.name: Drink & Draw
candidates.summary: A weekly drop-in sketching activity run by the Asheville Art Museum's rooftop Perspective Café: paper-covered tables and unlocked art supplies for anyone who makes a café purchase (museum admission required). It is an institutional program, not a self-organized group of returning artists.
aliases: Drink & Draw at Perspective Café (Asheville Art Museum)
candidates.notes: Asheville Art Museum's Drink & Draw at Perspective Cafe

candidates.name: Shakedown Sundays
candidates.summary: Shakedown Sundays is a weekly Grateful Dead-themed show at The One Stop / Asheville Music Hall: a house band set (rotating musician lineup) followed by an open jam for drop-in musicians. It is produced by Independent Arts and Music of Asheville (IAMAVL), a 501(c)3, and documented weekly on YouTube, not run by a self-identified membership community.

candidates.name: Eda's Hide-a-Way Pool Night
candidates.summary: A weekly $5 buy-in pool tournament run by the bar Eda's Hide-a-Way in Weaverville, sign-ups due by 7pm each Monday. It reads as a standard barroom house tournament rather than an organized club: there is no league name, no membership language, and no dedicated group page separate from the venue itself.

candidates.name: LGBTQ+ Improv Workshop
candidates.summary: A free monthly improv workshop for LGBTQ+ participants, run by Misfit Improv (an Asheville improv/acting school) and hosted at Campaign for Southern Equality's Southern Equality Studios, with proceeds from optional donations benefiting that nonprofit. Every session across 15 listed dates is led by the same two named Misfit facilitators, Megan Piscitelle and Stevie Ramirez, but the listings describe it as a drop-in class open to newcomers each time rather than a group with continuing membership.
candidates.notes: Misfit Improv with the Campaign for Southern Equality

candidates.name: Meetup Mondays at Archetype
candidates.summary: "Meetup Mondays" is Archetype Brewing's own weekly branded programming block (Mondays 7-10pm), not a single group of people. It rotates between different activities run by different organizers: a weekly craft night done with the Keep Asheville Crafty group, alternating Brazilian Roda drum/song circles, and a Meetup.com-organized Singles Game Night. The host (the brewery) recurs every week, but the activity and attendee base rotate, matching a venue promotion rather than one returning community.
candidates.notes: Archetype Brewing Monday program that rotates hosts

candidates.name: IBN Biz Lunch - West Asheville
candidates.summary: IBN is a free, sponsor-funded monthly networking lunch series run by Incredible Towns of WNC, a marketing/advertising agency, held across many WNC towns (this unit is the West Asheville chapter at a Smokey Park Highway buffet). The organizer explicitly advertises it as open to all with no membership, dues, or exclusions, so while some local business owners likely return often, there is no defined roster or membership structure, and the listings themselves only ever describe the rotating pitch of "all are invited to attend and promote their business."
aliases: Incredible Business Networking (IBN) Biz Lunch - West Asheville
candidates.notes: West Asheville chapter of Incredible Business Networking

candidates.name: IBN Biz Lunch - Brevard/Pisgah Forest
candidates.summary: IBN Biz Lunch is a free monthly business-networking lunch run by Incredible Towns of WNC, a regional media/events company that hosts near-identical IBN lunches at many WNC locations (Asheville east/west, Candler, Hendersonville, Brevard/Pisgah Forest, etc.), funded by sponsor businesses like Mr. Rooter Plumbing. The Brevard/Pisgah Forest edition meets the second Thursday monthly at Hawg Wild Smokehouse & Taproom. Every listing and the organizer's own site emphasize no membership, no dues, no attendance requirements, and an explicitly rotating/open model meant to keep welcoming new participants rather than a fixed roster of regulars.
aliases: Incredible Business Networking (IBN) - Brevard/Pisgah Forest chapter
candidates.notes: Brevard/Pisgah Forest chapter of Incredible Business Networking

candidates.name: Second Saturday Salons at Jeffrey Burroughs
candidates.summary: Jeffrey Burroughs is a fine jewelry and design boutique at 20 Artful Way in Asheville's River Arts District. Its 'Second Saturday Salon' is a monthly retail open house where the studio previews new jewelry and fragrance collections with light bites and champagne; it is part of the River Arts District's broader 'Second Saturday' shopping event. Only the host business recurs, and attendees are walk-in shoppers, collectors, and visitors rather than a fixed membership.
aliases: Second Saturday Salons at Jeffrey Burroughs (boutique open house)

candidates.name: Free Mary Magdalene Meditation Circle
candidates.summary: A free virtual monthly meditation webinar hosted solo by Adora Winquist of The Soul Institute, cross-posted to Eventbrite under near-identical city-tagged listings (AVL, New York, St. Louis, and many other cities) for local SEO/ad targeting. All three listings share the exact same location field 'Virtual, Asheville, NC' and the identical first-person-singular description ('I invite you to meditate with me...'), indicating one host running one recurring session, not distinct local communities. It functions as a lead-generation funnel into Adora's paid retreats and membership, not a returning-member circle.
aliases: Free Mary Magdalene Meditation Circle (The Soul Institute / Adora Winquist)
candidates.notes: The Soul Institute / Adora Winquist; listed separately per city

candidates.name: Girls' Craft Night
candidates.summary: A weekly drop-in craft night at Sidetracked Brewery in Morganton, NC (over an hour from Asheville), run by an Eventbrite organizer account called "Julie's Craft Café" that sells generic templated craft-night listings. There is no membership language, named regulars, or community platform, and the identical marketing copy repeats verbatim across all nine weekly listings, consistent with a commercial drop-in series rather than a returning community.

candidates.name: Intentional Conversations
candidates.summary: "Intentional Conversations" is a weekly internal sales-training session for Keller Williams Professionals real estate agents, held at the brokerage's Learning Lab at 48 Grove St, Asheville. Eventbrite listings dress it up in generic community/connection marketing copy, but the actual content is agent skill-building on listing presentations and handling seller objections (e.g. pricing, lockboxes). It is company training with a rotating audience of agents, not a persistent social group.

candidates.name: Modern Local ARTSOUP
candidates.summary: Modern Local ARTSOUP is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit gallery in Mars Hill supporting Appalachian artists; its Friday night 'ArtSoup' sessions are the venue's own recurring open-to-the-public programming (dance parties, tabletop games, live music, free hot soup, local sourdough and bagels), tied to Mars Hill's First Fridays but listed weekly. It is run by the gallery/nonprofit itself rather than by a club, and nothing in the listings or the org's own pages frames it as a membership community with returning regulars.

candidates.name: Wild Food Community Walks
candidates.summary: A paid guided foraging/nature-connection walk series run by Foraging Home, a one-guide business (Bek) in Asheville. Walks are sold as single sessions ($25-$275 depending on package) or discounted multi-session series, with no membership structure, dues, or self-organizing group identity described anywhere.

candidates.name: Drumming for Fitness
candidates.summary: A weekly low-impact fitness class at Harvest House Community Center, a City of Asheville Parks & Recreation senior center, where participants drum along to music for an arm/core workout. It is a rec-center program alongside Chair Volleyball, Chair Aerobics and Tai Chi, run by Parks & Recreation staff rather than by a self-organized group, with no membership language, named leader, or regular-attendee identity in the listings.
candidates.notes: listed as Drumming for Exercise at Harvest House

candidates.name: Morning Mingle
candidates.summary: A monthly coffee mixer held inside Keller Williams Professionals' own office at 48 Grove Street, Asheville, explicitly for "agents to get to know other agents." It is an internal networking/team-building event run by a single real estate brokerage for its own agents, not a chapter or club with membership drawn from multiple businesses or the public.

candidates.name: Escape to the Page
candidates.summary: Escape to the Page is a paid creative writing class using a 'Wild Writing' prompt technique, led by writer/teacher Sondra Hall, held at Muse Art Bar in this listing (an 8-week Monday series, $280 upfront) and separately as $35 drop-in sessions at other venues like Blind Tiger and White Horse Black Mountain. It is a commercial class taught by one instructor across multiple venues, not a fixed-membership community, despite 'writing in community' framing.
aliases: Escape to the Page (creative writing workshop, run by Sondra Hall)
candidates.notes: creative writing workshop run by Sondra Hall

candidates.name: Queer-Led Mushroom Forage
candidates.summary: This is a recurring, ticketed guided mushroom-foraging tour run by a single host ("Doctor Delia"), sold as individual paid experiences ($18-$29, some free dates) on Eventbrite. Each listing repeats identical boilerplate about songs, chants, and a 'mushroom dance,' with no membership language, sign-up form, dues, named regulars, or links to a Facebook/Meetup/Discord group. It reads as a commercial, queer-themed nature tour rather than a persistent community with returning members.

candidates.name: Foodies + New Friends Asheville
candidates.summary: A ticketed ($31), monthly dinner meetup run by Ermantourage (by ADDVentures), a commercial event-production company operating the same 'Foodies + New Friends' format across 9+ cities nationwide (Hendersonville, Roseville, Fayetteville, Charlottesville, Los Angeles, etc.), each with rotating themed editions (Giving Back, Single Friends, 1-on-1). Attendees sign up individually per dinner for small tables of 4-6 to 12-24 strangers; there is no fixed membership, roster, or evidence of the same people returning across sessions in Asheville. The recurrence is the company's franchise-style event product, not a persistent local community.

candidates.name: Oak and Grist Game Night
candidates.summary: A weekly bring-your-own board/card/RPG game night hosted by Oak and Grist Distilling Co. in its Black Mountain taproom, alongside their other recurring offerings like trivia and live music. There is no dedicated identity, membership language, or organizing body beyond the venue; descriptions are generic ('settle in for a fun night with friends') and never mention returning regulars or named leaders.

candidates.name: Honky Tonk Dance Hall
candidates.summary: A free monthly dance night presented by the venue Foothills Watershed (Old Fort, NC, near Asheville) together with 'Slow Down Sound w/ Old School Dance Hall', featuring a 30-minute line dancing/two-step lesson followed by open dancing to a live band, plus food trucks and local beer. It reads as a recurring venue event night rather than a bounded community: no membership language, sign-up form, Facebook group for attendees, or named regulars appears anywhere.
candidates.notes: Watershed / Foothills Local Meats dance nights

candidates.name: Cherry St Doggie Ice Cream Social
candidates.summary: A monthly promotional pop-up co-hosted by two neighboring Cherry St businesses in downtown Black Mountain: The Hop Ice Cream Cafe and Bone-A-Fide Pet Boutique. Dogs get free 'Happy Tails' doggie ice cream with a $10+ purchase at The Hop, plus treats/activities from the pet boutique, held in the courtyard between the two shops. It reads as a recurring commercial promotion (like a drink/treat special) rather than a club with a defined membership; attendees are simply neighborhood dog owners dropping in, not a named, returning cohort.
aliases: Doggie Ice Cream Social Series (The Hop x Bone-A-Fide Pet Boutique)
candidates.notes: The Hop with Bone-A-Fide Pet Boutique

candidates.name: Primal Scream Club
candidates.summary: Primal Scream Club is a drop-in wellness program run by Buncombe County Public Libraries (West Asheville Library, librarian Erin Parcels), now hosted monthly on New Belgium Brewing's river deck. It began as a one-time Helene-anniversary healing gathering in September 2025 and became a recurring library program; listings explicitly say 'no registration required, just show up,' with no membership structure, dues, or sign-up mentioned.

candidates.name: Hickory Nut Gap Barn Dance
candidates.summary: A monthly ticketed dance night run by Hickory Nut Gap Farm (owned by Jamie and Amy Ager) in their barn in Fairview, featuring a rotating lineup of local bluegrass/old-time/swing/Cajun bands, food trucks, and a bar. The farm intentionally varies the music and dance style (square dance with caller, swing, zydeco) week to week to draw different crowds rather than cultivate a fixed membership, and the event is explicitly sold and marketed as a commercial farm attraction, not a dance club.
aliases: Hickory Nut Gap Farm Barn Dance (Friday Night Barn Dance series)
candidates.notes: Friday Night Barn Dance series at Hickory Nut Gap Farm

candidates.name: Open Page: A Meditative Writing Circle
candidates.summary: A biweekly meditative free-writing session hosted at Quietude, a retreat/event venue in Black Mountain, NC, teaching continuous stream-of-consciousness writing as a healing practice. Listings are organized by "Quietude" itself (the venue), are ticketed ($5-$20 sliding scale), and are pitched as beginner-friendly and open to "creatives" and anyone with writer's block, with no language distinguishing returning participants from newcomers.

candidates.name: The Artist's Way
candidates.summary: A paid 12-week creativity course based on Julia Cameron's 'The Artist's Way' book, run as a commercial continuing-education offering by Still Point Wellness Float and Massage Spa in Asheville, facilitated by two named instructors (Robin Fann-Costanzo and Samata DeCori). It is capped at 10 students, costs $525 plus supplies, and enrollment is by signing up for 'our next offering' - a closed paying cohort for one course run, not an ongoing open community members return to indefinitely.
aliases: The Artist's Way (12-week course at Still Point Wellness)

candidates.name: Romancing the Muse
candidates.summary: A monthly drop-in creative-writing workshop at Story Parlor, facilitated by writer/performer R Lyon Bergh as part of the venue's 'Sunday Sessions' programming. It blends timed writing prompts, light movement/meditation, and optional group sharing, but is explicitly free and open to the public rather than a membership-based community.
aliases: Romancing the Muse: Sunday Edition (Story Parlor Sunday Sessions)

candidates.name: Wyrding Women
candidates.summary: "Wyrding Women's Rhythmic Immersion" is a six-class frame drum instructional series taught by Brandi Mizilca, a professional dancer/drummer/healing-arts practitioner, held at The Well (associated with Arts2People) in Asheville. "Wyrding women" is descriptive language for the participants ("female and female-identifying humans"), not the name of a pre-existing standing group; the listing frames it as a paid, enrollment-based class with a minimum headcount, not an ongoing circle with independent membership.
candidates.notes: frame drum immersion at The Well

candidates.name: Trackside Studios Life Drawing
candidates.summary: A monthly untutored figure-drawing session with a live nude model, run as a paid, individually bookable session at Trackside Studios, a commercial art gallery/studio in the River Arts District. There is no membership language, roster, or affiliated Facebook/Meetup group tied specifically to the session, and the studio's own site presents it as a 'Book Now' class alongside its other paid classes rather than a standing community.

candidates.name: IBN Biz Lunch - East Asheville
candidates.summary: A free, drop-in monthly business networking lunch run by Incredible Towns of WNC, normally held the first Tuesday of the month (recently at Red Lobster on Tunnel Road, currently seeking a new venue). Its own promotional copy states it is 'open to all, with never any dues, fees, restrictions, exclusions, or membership requirements' - you just show up and buy lunch. This matches the finding for the sibling IBN chapters (Woodfin, Asheville West, Brevard/Pisgah Forest): a rotating public of local business people rather than a fixed membership.
aliases: Incredible Business Networking (IBN) - East Asheville chapter
candidates.notes: East Asheville chapter of Incredible Business Networking

candidates.name: IBN Evening Social - WNC
candidates.summary: A monthly after-hours business mixer run by Steve Jencks' company Incredible Towns of WNC, held at 12 Bones Brewing in Arden. It is explicitly free, open to all, with no dues, fees, membership requirements, or exclusions, and is one of several interchangeable IBN formats (breakfast, lunch, dinner, evening social) rotating across WNC towns rather than a fixed-membership chapter with a returning core.
candidates.notes: regional evening social of Incredible Business Networking

candidates.name: Misfit Improv and Acting School
candidates.summary: Misfit Improv & Acting School is a commercial improv/acting school in Asheville founded by Gillian Bellinger, offering paid tiered classes, corporate workshops, and coaching, plus free community outreach events including a quarterly 'Jam Jam' drop-in improv night. The Jam Jam itself is an open, name-drawn-from-a-bucket format explicitly welcoming newcomers and spectators, not a fixed roster of returning players.
candidates.notes: runs the Improv All Play jam

candidates.name: Scribbles of Strength
candidates.summary: Scribbles of Strength is a touring therapeutic creative-writing workshop created and led by a single facilitator, Emily Marjean Coolbeth, who books it as a one-time paid session at different host venues around the country (Story Parlor in Asheville, The Reading Attic in Marietta GA, Thought Fox in Stonington CT, and now Full Circle Community Wellness in Hendersonville). The Hendersonville listings just happen to recur monthly at the same host venue, but each session is a self-contained $20 ticketed class with no membership language, sign-up roster, or community identity - it is the facilitator's brand that recurs, not a body of attendees.
aliases: Scribbles of Strength: Write to Heal (workshop by Emily Marjean Coolbeth)
candidates.notes: Write to Heal workshop by Emily Marjean Coolbeth

candidates.name: Creativity Mixer: Narrative Arts Salon
candidates.summary: A monthly ticketed workshop-and-open-mic hybrid produced by Story Parlor (a West Asheville performance venue) and led by a rotating certified 'Inward & Artward' Creative Facilitator, the training program run by Story Parlor's own founder Erin Hallagan Clare. The second half is an open-floor share round with a sign-up sheet at the door for whoever shows up, not a fixed membership sharing work with familiar peers.

candidates.name: Root & Rise
candidates.summary: Root & Rise is a monthly ticketed ceremonial gathering at The Well in West Asheville, led by two named facilitators (Sinclair Fleetwood, a psychedelic integration coach/ceremonialist, and Ian Campbell, a shamanic energy healer and Gene Keys guide). Each session rotates in format (cacao ceremony, shamanic journeywork, somatic movement, yoga nidra) and is booked individually via a sliding-scale ($44-$77) Google Form, with no membership structure described.
candidates.notes: monthly cacao ceremony and shamanic journey at The Well

candidates.name: Rooftop Salsa
candidates.summary: A recurring salsa night run directly by Highland Brewing Company on its rooftop: a beginner-friendly salsa lesson (no partner needed) followed by two hours of open social dancing, held only sparsely (3 times over ~4 months). No dance school, instructor, or community organization is named anywhere in the listings or on the web; it reads as brewery-run themed programming rather than a standing dance community with its own identity.

candidates.name: Craft & Chill
candidates.summary: Craft & Chill is Plant Bar West Asheville's own promotional weekly hangout: bring-your-own-supplies painting, sketching, and knitting while drinking at the bar. It is run and branded entirely by the venue, not by an independent organizer or club, and the listings invite guests to bring friends rather than referencing returning members.

candidates.name: The Pocket Project
candidates.summary: The Pocket Project is a monthly free creativity workshop hosted at Story Parlor and facilitated solely by Alli Marshall, a certified Inward & Artward creative facilitator. It is drop-in, ticketless programming ('Sunday Sessions are FREE to the public. Come as you are') with no membership, dues, sign-up roster, or dedicated community channel (Facebook group/Meetup/Discord) of its own -- only the facilitator and the Story Parlor venue recur, not a fixed set of attendees.
candidates.notes: with Alli Marshall at Story Parlor

candidates.name: True Stories: A Ritual For Telling & Listening
candidates.summary: A monthly Sunday-morning storytelling and active-listening practice at Story Parlor in West Asheville, part of the venue's recurring "Sunday Sessions" program slate alongside other facilitator-led offerings like "Our Shared Creative Practice" and "Romancing the Muse." The listing URL slug ("...arnold-sundaysession...") points to a named facilitator running the session, not a self-identified membership group. All three months' descriptions are near-identical boilerplate describing the practice itself ("we'll practice how to communicate our stories concisely... and listen with acceptance and empathy") with no membership language, no mention of regulars, no link to a Facebook group/Meetup/Discord, and it is ticketed rather than free-to-join.

candidates.name: Spirited Improv
candidates.summary: Spirited Improv is a paid 6-week playshop series ("Sacred Playshop" / nighttime series) run by a single facilitator, expressive arts therapist Jessica Chilton, operating as SPARK Creative Wellness Studio, LLC, held at 83 Sanctuary Road in Swannanoa. It is structured and marketed as a commercial class series (registration fee, work-trade option) rather than a self-organized club, though the site notes many participants return across series and "deepen into the Spirited Improv community over the years." Could not confirm any independent Meetup group ("Awakening Asheville") actually hosting or affiliated with this series; the group's Meetup page could not be located.
aliases: Spirited Improv (SPARK Creative Wellness Studio, LLC)

candidates.name: Conversational Spanish Class
candidates.summary: A free drop-in Spanish-speaking practice class run by Bounty & Soul, a Black Mountain/Swannanoa food and wellness nonprofit, held weekly Mondays at the Beacon Community Center and sponsored by White Horse Community Hub. It is framed as instruction ('this class is designed for people who want to speak Spanish') with explicitly no registration and no named instructor, alongside similar offerings like a 'Beginner English Class' on the same org's calendar, suggesting an institutional language-class program rather than a self-identified community of returning members.
candidates.notes: Bounty & Soul at Beacon Community Center

candidates.name: Weaverville Library Teen Dungeons & Dragons
candidates.summary: A Buncombe County Library program at the Weaverville branch offering Dungeons & Dragons sessions for tweens/teens ages 12-18, run by library staff. Both listed sessions describe it identically as open to 'all skill levels' with simple phone/in-person registration required only because space is limited, not because of a fixed roster. No campaign, membership, DM name, or outside community presence (Facebook, Discord, Meetup) is referenced anywhere.

candidates.name: Ridge Runout Gravel
candidates.summary: A ticketed ($71), self-supported gravel cycling ride series held at a reservation-only farm/forest retreat near Newland, NC, presented by WILDHAVEN Farm & Forest Retreat host Cass Bradley in partnership with Overmountain Cycles bike shop, benefiting the Northwest NC Mountain Bike Alliance. It reads as a recurring commercial/charity ride event rather than a club with a defined membership: riders register and pay per ride, with post-ride beer and food framed as "community" but no sign-up list, dues, or member roster.

candidates.name: Come to Leicester
candidates.summary: "Come to Leicester" is the brand name of an annual self-guided artist studio tour held every third weekend of August in Leicester, NC, not a standing membership association. Its own website describes it as an annual community event where a rotating "community of artists" open their studios to the public; there is no mention of dues, a member roster, or an organizing club, and a PayPal link is for "Artist and Sponsor Payments" (participation fees), similar to a fair or vendor event.

candidates.name: Coven Divine
candidates.summary: Coven Divine is a solo spiritual practitioner's business led by 'Ceremonial Priestess' Alessandra Mary, offering ticketed ($34) New Moon ceremonies plus paid courses, candles, and a book anthology across multiple NC towns (Mars Hill, Burnsville, Weaverville, Asheville). Despite the 'coven' name and 'Coven Gathering' tag, the site's own framing is client/service-based (a newsletter and purchasable offerings), not a membership circle with dues or a fixed roster.

candidates.name: Intergenerational LEGO Club
candidates.summary: A staff-run, drop-in LEGO building program hosted biweekly at the East Asheville branch of the Buncombe County Public Library. It is open to all ages with library-supplied bricks and no membership, sign-up, or dues; attendees are a rotating public rather than a fixed set of returning members.

candidates.name: Table 4 Tonight Hendersonville
candidates.summary: A ticketed ($29), monthly dinner meetup at a rotating 'Restaurant of the Week' in Hendersonville, run by Ermantourage Sports as part of its 'Dinner with Strangers' brand, explicitly targeted at 'cities under 100,000 population.' It is the same commercial event-production company (Ermantourage) confirmed elsewhere to run the near-identical 'Foodies + New Friends' series across 9+ cities nationwide as a booking product, not a persistent local community.

candidates.name: Dancing on the Square
candidates.summary: A free Friday-night outdoor square dance series on the Robbinsville, NC courthouse square, run by Graham County Travel and Tourism as a summer tourism draw for locals and visitors (May-August, with two America 250 marquee dates). Both listings describe a 'mix of returning favorites and new performers' -- i.e. rotating callers/bands booked by the tourism office -- with no mention of a dancer membership, club, sign-up, or dues; the recurring elements are the host organization and the performer lineup, not a fixed community of attendees.

candidates.name: IBN Breakfast Club - Mills River
candidates.summary: A monthly free breakfast networking event at Mills River Restaurant, run by Incredible Towns of WNC as part of its Incredible Business Networking (IBN) program. Both event listings and the parent organization's site explicitly state it is open to all with no dues, fees, or membership requirements, matching the five other IBN chapters already evaluated as open drop-in networking rather than a fixed-membership group.
aliases: IBN Breakfast Club – Mills River NC
candidates.notes: Mills River chapter of Incredible Business Networking

candidates.name: Kanuga Celtic Eucharist Hikes
candidates.summary: A free, Eventbrite-ticketed contemplative hike across Kanuga's campus trails ending in a Celtic-style Eucharist, offered by Kanuga itself (an Episcopal non-profit conference, retreat and camp center near Hendersonville hosting roughly 35,000 guests a year). Only two dates on record, 70 days apart, with no membership language, named leaders/regulars, or dedicated program page found.

candidates.name: Mary Plantwalker Earth Devotion Gatherings
candidates.summary: Ticketed seasonal ceremony ('Winter Solstice Earth Devotion Gathering') held at Herb Mountain Farm in Weaverville, NC, led by a single named individual, Mary Plantwalker, featuring an herbal tea ceremony, wild-edibles ID, and craft-making. The listings and organizer page show no group name, no membership language, and no social/community links; it reads as a solo practitioner's paid seasonal offering rather than a club with a fixed, returning membership.

candidates.name: Mudpuppies Bike Night
candidates.summary: A monthly bike night hosted by Mudpuppies Sports Bar and Grill (last Thursday of the month, 4-9pm) with reserved rider parking and food/drink specials. It is a bar promotion open to any local biker who wants to show up, not a named motorcycle club or riding group with a defined membership.

candidates.name: Oakley/South Asheville Library LEGO Club
candidates.summary: A Buncombe County Public Library drop-in LEGO building program held at the Murphy-Oakley Community Center, hosted by the Oakley/South Asheville branch on the first and third Saturday of each month. The library supplies the bricks and explicitly asks attendees to leave personal LEGO sets at home, and the listings use no membership, sign-up, or dues language, just an open invitation to 'families and builders.' It is staff-run programming for a rotating public rather than a persistent group with returning members.

candidates.name: Nightshade Game Night
candidates.summary: A free Sunday 4-8 PM drop-in game night hosted by Nightshade, a non-alcoholic social lounge in South Slope, Asheville, where guests can play the house collection of board/card games or bring their own. There is no membership language, sign-up, or club identity in the listings, and the venue's own website doesn't mention game night as a program at all, focusing instead on DJ sets and live music - this reads as a one-off/occasional venue promo, matching the sibling venue game nights (Hi-Wire, RAD Brewing, Oak and Grist, Plant Bar) already classified not_group.

candidates.name: Plant Bar Game Night
candidates.summary: A weekly Wednesday bring-your-own-or-borrow board and card game night hosted by Plant Bar - South Slope in its own taproom, framed as a casual bar promotion ("Grab a friend, grab a game...and grab a drink") rather than a club with members. No membership language, sign-up, or linked community (Facebook group, Discord, etc.) appears in the listings or on the venue's event page, which only offers a general newsletter signup.

candidates.name: Red Tent Workshop & Cacao Ceremony
candidates.summary: A ticketed ($29-$34) workshop and cacao ceremony hosted by a single named practitioner, Priscilla Jordan, at Asia House Asheville. Only two sessions were listed 3 months apart, with 'Red Tent' and 'sacred circle' used as marketing language rather than as the name of an established, independently branded community. No membership language, group name, or dedicated web/social presence for the group was found.

candidates.name: Our Shared Creative Practice
candidates.summary: A free, drop-in creative-practice session facilitated by Andy Collins (of Inward & Artward School of Creativity) as part of Story Parlor's recurring 'Sunday Sessions' program. The event's own listing describes it as a recurring entry in that program with an explicit 'come as you are' open-attendance invitation, no mention of membership, dues, or a stable roster of participants.

candidates.name: Valley Hope Church
candidates.summary: A weekly bilingual (English/Spanish) free community meal hosted by Valley Hope Church at 115 Rockdale Ave, Swannanoa, NC. The listings frame it as an open, welcoming meal for 'neighbors' in the area rather than a gathering of a defined membership; it reads as the church's charitable outreach/service rather than a club-like community with recurring identifiable members.
